title: Multimodal and Multiscale Interrogation of a Mechanically Tough Glass Forming Copper-Based Metal-Organic Framework
authors: Mounir El Skafi, Guo-Qiang Li, Sophie R. Thomas, James D. Taylor, Mark Frogley, Gianfelice Cinque, Marc Pignitter, Michael Reithofer, Jia-Min Chin, Sebastian Henke, Jin-Chong Tan
abstract: A copper-based metal-organic framework, Cu(Im)2, was synthesized using a sol-gel process and subsequently melt-quenched into glass upon heating above 240 °C. In this paper, we present a multimodal, multiscale interrogation of the MOF nanocrystals and the resulting glasses. Structural characterization using X-ray diffraction, atomic force microscopy, and electron microscopy was performed to understand the morphology and size of the synthesized nanocrystals and glasses. Thermogravimetric analysis and differential scanning calorimetry were employed to understand the melting process of the crystals to form the glass. Synchrotron pair distribution function analysis was performed to verify that the framework structure is maintained upon melting, and nearfield infrared nanospectroscopy provided insight into the local chemical structure of the materials. The mechanical characterization via nanoindentation revealed that the resulting glasses exhibit an appreciably high elastic modulus (~10 GPa) and the highest fracture toughness (K_1c ~ 0.5 MPa m^1/2) yet reported for MOF glasses. This development is central to the emerging field of MOF-based materials processing and shaping, while upholding mechanical robustness and resistance to cracking.
summary: This work thoroughly characterizes a copper-based MOF that forms a glass upon heating. By using multiple advanced techniques, the researchers demonstrated that the resulting glass possesses exceptional mechanical robustness, achieving high stiffness and record-high fracture toughness for MOF glasses. This advances the field of processing and shaping MOF-derived materials.
main_problem: To conduct a multimodal and multiscale interrogation of a mechanically tough, glass-forming copper-based Metal-Organic Framework (MOF).
main_result: The resulting MOF glasses exhibit an appreciably high elastic modulus (~10 GPa) and the highest fracture toughness (K_Ic ~ 0.5 MPa m^1/2) reported for MOF glasses.
method: The study employed a combination of structural, thermal, and mechanical characterization techniques, including XRD, AFM, nanoindentation, and synchrotron pair distribution function analysis.
model_or_system: The physical system is a copper-based MOF, Cu(Im)2, which is synthesized and subsequently melt-quenched into a glass state upon heating above 240 °C.
key_observables: Elastic modulus (E), fracture toughness (K_Ic), BET surface areas, and structural motifs observed via various microscopy and spectroscopy techniques.
important_parameters: Melting temperatures (e.g., 240 °C to 310 °C), quenching times, and mechanical stress/strain regimes.
main_assumptions: The mechanical properties are compared against literature examples, and the study focuses on the structural integrity of the framework upon glass formation.
figures_summary: Figures show images of as-synthesized crystals and melted glass samples, and supplementary figures detail R-STEM micrographs, THz spectroscopy, and nanoindentation results.
paper_structure: The paper follows a comprehensive characterization approach, detailing structural analysis (XRD, microscopy, synchrotron methods), thermal analysis (TGA/DSC), and culminating in mechanical testing (nanoindentation, K_Ic measurement).
why_interesting: While the focus is on materials science, the study of glass formation and mechanical failure in complex, porous frameworks touches upon concepts relevant to disordered systems and amorphous materials physics.
